name: variable-font-and-cursor

frames.best_why: The word is bold and upright with both crosshair guides and the coordinate readout visible at once.

tagline: Moving the cursor changes the word's weight and slant.
summary: A single word whose thickness and slant follow the mouse across its container, with faint crosshair guides and a live x and y readout tracking the pointer.
appearance: An orange lowercase word sits centred on a black full-bleed stage. Faint grey crosshair lines and a tiny orange dot follow the pointer, with a small monospaced x and y readout at the lower left.
behaviour: As the pointer moves, the word's weight and slant interpolate between set limits, sliding from hairline to heavy and upright to italic. The crosshair lines and coordinates travel with the cursor.
demo_content: The word stash! in orange, with live x and y coordinates beneath it
search_phrases: text that changes weight with mouse
word gets bolder as you move
use_when: A portfolio or agency headline wants an interactive typographic moment that rewards moving the pointer.
avoid_when: Essential copy, since it needs a pointer and thins the text until it nearly disappears at one end.
customise: Children are the text; fontVariationMapping picks which axis each cursor direction drives and its range, and containerRef sets the tracking area. The variable font itself must be loaded elsewhere.
weight_why: One text node restyled on each animation frame; no canvas or heavy node count.

a11y.note: Purely pointer-driven, so keyboard users get no equivalent, and no reduced-motion preference is checked.

issues: At the lightest setting the word turns hairline and almost vanishes against the black stage.
polish_why: Sharp variable type and a clear crosshair; the bare demo and near-invisible light end lower it.
